features.title: Add workspaces from the folder browser
features.summary: The header and sidebar Add workspace flows open directly in the Host-backed folder explorer without offering registered projects; one unique typed folder match browses automatically. Browse… opens the Host's native folder dialog when its directory picker is native, and the workspace_folder_browser_capabilities agent tool reports that, with the Host's path style, without opening it. Choosing a folder first reports what it is: no repository, a Git checkout with its origin and default branch, or a Jujutsu repository. A Git checkout offers Enable Jujutsu and add, which runs the same guarded colocated init the graph uses; a folder without a repository offers Initialize repository, which starts Jujutsu in place and keeps the files already in it. The project_inspect and project_init agent tools drive the same read and write. A repository can also check in dsh.project.json, read by project_config_read: icon path, default thread workspace, bookmark, trusted check ids and suggested scripts, where a missing or invalid file is reported instead of thrown. A repository with no origin says so and offers Publish privately or Publish publicly, which creates the GitHub repository, adds it as origin and pushes the bookmark. Settings › Projects shows the same file for a registered project: the declared values, the tier that wins for each key, and a Copy entry button per suggested script, which copies the trusted project-checks profile entry because nothing is imported automatically.
failureModes: Directory listing and folder creation use an authenticated Host API; workspace registration stays behind the workspace Remote API.
Ambiguous or truncated path matches do not auto-browse.
The add flow does not expose registered project choices or project registration actions.
A Host without a native directory picker, or one too old to answer the capability read, hides Browse… and keeps absolute-path entry and the in-app browser.
Cancelling the native dialog changes nothing; a failed dialog keeps absolute-path entry and offers Browse… again.
The setup step never initializes a repository by itself: every write follows an explicit click.
A folder already inside a checkout is reported with that checkout's root, and adding it registers the folder you chose.
Enable Jujutsu is offered only while the Jujutsu bundle is loaded and jj is installed; otherwise the panel offers the plain add and says why.
A folder with broken .jj metadata is reported as broken and is never repaired or replaced.
Initialize repository refuses a folder that is already a repository or sits inside one, naming the checkout to add instead.
Only non-executable settings from dsh.project.json are honoured: a script runs only after the user imports it into the profile-trusted project checks.
The project settings section only reads dsh.project.json: it never imports a script or runs a command from the file.

features.title: Add a project by cloning a repository
features.summary: New → Clone repository… in the Add workspace flow clones an https, ssh or file:// repository into a new folder in the background with git stage progress (connecting, counting, receiving, resolving, checkout) and a Cancel button, colocates jj when it is installed, registers the clone as a project and selects it. A failed or cancelled job can be retried into the same folder as a new job; a clone that failed after git started checking files out keeps that partial tree, and its retry clears it first. Closing the dialog does not hide a running or failed clone: a shell overlaid notice keeps its phase, Cancel and Retry on screen. The project_clone, project_clone_jobs, project_clone_cancel and project_clone_retry agent tools drive the same jobs.
features.currentSurface: composer: Choose workspace › Add workspace › Clone repository
failureModes: An existing destination folder is refused before anything runs; a second start for the same folder returns the running job.

A failed clone before git checks files out deletes the folder it created and registers nothing; a clone that failed during or after checkout keeps its partial tree and names the retry that clears it, and a failed jj colocation keeps the clone and names the command to finish it.
Clone jobs live in Host memory: a Host restart drops the trail, and a clone it interrupted leaves its partial folder.

keeps a checkout that failed after it started, then retries clean into the same folder
announces running and undismissed failed clones, newest first and at most three

features.title: Create a new project
features.summary: New → New project… in the Add workspace flow creates <parent>/<name> with a colocated jj repository, a README, a described first commit on main, registers it as a project and selects it. Opting in to a private GitHub repository runs gh repo create --private and pushes main when the GitHub CLI is installed. The project_create agent tool takes the same explicit inputs. The same remote creation is available for an existing checkout through project_publish: it refuses no-repository, an existing origin, and a repository without commits, then pushes the bookmark with jj (git for a plain checkout).

features.title: Inspect a folder before adding it
features.summary: Choosing a folder opens a step that says what it is — no repository, a Git checkout with its origin, or a Jujutsu repository, and whether its .jj metadata is broken — before anything is registered. A Git checkout offers Enable Jujutsu and add, a plain folder offers Initialize repository or Add without a repository, and a repository with no origin offers Publish privately or Publish publicly. Nothing is written without the click, and the plain add stays available for every folder.
failureModes: The step never initializes or enables anything by itself: every write follows an explicit click.
A folder with broken .jj metadata is reported and never repaired or replaced.
A folder inside another checkout is reported with that checkout root; adding still registers the folder chosen.
Enable Jujutsu is offered only while the Jujutsu bundle is loaded and jj is installed.
Publishing needs the GitHub CLI; a refusal names the missing tool or the next command instead of failing silently.

externalDependencies.boundary: Colocated Jujutsu init behind the repository-setup contract.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: A fake provider returning a fixed root.

features.title: Read a project's declared settings
features.summary: Settings › Projects lists the Host's registered projects, leaving out jj thread workspaces, and reads the chosen project's dsh.project.json. Each declared key shows its value and the tier that wins: the file when it declares the key, the profile setting for the new-thread workspace and bookmark, and a built-in default otherwise. A missing or invalid file is reported without changing anything. Each suggested script offers Copy entry, which puts the exact trusted project-checks profile entry on the clipboard for an operator to paste; nothing is imported automatically and the file never runs a command. The project_projects agent tool lists the same projects.
failureModes: The section only reads: it imports no script and runs no command from dsh.project.json.
A missing file shows the profile and built-in tiers instead of an error; an invalid file is reported and changes nothing.
A command line that cannot be split into an executable and its arguments is reported and its copy button stays disabled.
An old Host without the projects method shows the read failure with a retry instead of an empty project list.
